To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Android emulators can be detected with a very high accuracy (99.7%) using instruction level profiles and (ii) we have discovered 3 major classes (and many sub-classes) of root causes that lead to the divergence between emulators and real CPUs.

1) we systematically discovered 28K divergences between ARM emulators and ARM CPUs; 2) we identified 3 major classes root causes for these discrepancies; 3) we found some of these root cases to be easily fixable without performance degradation in the emulators; 4) we proposed and implemented a system to automatically identify these divergent instruction instances and root causes; and 5) we submitted patches to fix the root cases that we identified.
we have uncovered 28K divergences in instruction level behavior of Android emulators and real CPUs.

we have developed the Proteus system which systematically uncovers the discrepancies in instruction level behaviors that occur between software based emulated environments and real ARM CPUs.
Proteus is the first work to uncover the root causes of instruction level divergence between software based Android emulators and ARM CPUs.

we present a new approach to detect emulated environment based on the instruction level behavior of the emulated and real environment.

instruction-level behavior of software emulators and real hardware is not always the same.
